brief: review
review

body: ADMINISTRATION.md's 'Live sprints' paragraph still describes test sprint boilerplate, admin/retired-test-sprint-boilerplate.json, and the -plan.json folders rewrite, which this stage removed from admin/true-up; i17-admin-doc (t61) owns the rewrite.

.ok-planner/review/project.md's scripts/tests entry lists the tool's inputs; this stage added the enabled and budget verbs and the --enabled and --offers flags, and the file lies outside this task's files (t63 i01-project-facts edits the entry). Harm: the review loop's facts omit the new inputs until that entry is updated.

skills/_sprint/shared.md:694 TEST-WASTE-RULE restates the testing standard's named wastes, and its setup waste lacks the clause 'or data the test only reads that the project's seed could hold' that docs/testing.md now carries; no stage's notes name this edit, so planners and verifiers reading the block miss the seed waste.

Old wall-time-charge wording ('ranked by what each adds to the run's wall time') stands at skills/converge/prompts/test-speed.md:9,17,59, skills/plan-sprint/tests-story.md:29, skills/plan-sprint/tests-runtime.md:79, scripts/tests:219,2429,2934, and families/ok-planner/CLAUDE.md:67; docs/testing.md now ranks by median seconds charged by the recorded schedule's lower bound. Stages t23, t41, t42, t44 own these files.

TEST-CALL-RULE defines the scope call kind as 'it reads the plan's scope or what a story covers', and scripts/tests CALL_KINDS keeps scope; item 3 retires the plan's scope, so the definition names a thing that no longer exists. The planner prompts no longer record scope calls.

tests-story.md:55 and tests-runtime.md:40 tell the planner to run .ok-planner/bin/tests window --json, which this stage retired (B102, B112); the verb now fails as an unknown choice. tests-sort.md (lines 9, 20-26, 65, 73, 108) still describes claimed test files a person edited and the claimed sort, which this stage retired. i03-planners owns these files.
plan-sprint/SKILL.md:115 still says a test sprint owns the tests and /plan-tests plans it; B119 moves test ownership to the sprint's test stages

scripts/ok-planner-cheatsheet.md, scripts/ok-planner-CLAUDE.md, and docs/plumbline-cheatsheet.md say dashboard, stack_helpers, and surface_corpus hold the limits, waits, and thresholds; archive.part_bytes is now a limit in .ok-planner/config.json they do not name, so an agent reading the rules does not learn the key or its reader (the task tracker's split).

tests-budget.md lines 28-30 still say a test is isolated unless it declares a resource it changes, and that the suite command runs a test that declares a resource holding it alone. Under item 8 the recommended schedule runs non-conflicting tests side by side and adds reads; the budget planner reads the retired rule.

test-verify.md's A test section includes {{TEST-SPEED-JUDGING}}, which now carries the product-slow verdict (item 6's build note: the write-time verifier may record it as the speed reviewer does), but offers only accept and sent-back on the tests item; it needs a product-slow line that adds a speed pool item (scenario, test, seconds, site, does, grows, cheaper) and says what becomes of the tests item. The file is t48 i11-prompts', outside this task.

checks/owned-paths fails on this stage: '[sys.executable, TESTS_SRC] + args' needs an entry (tests_command) beside intake_command's, and the filing_steps needle 'file_issues(pending + facts + docspecs)' must accept the added test-sprint issues (i17-config adds the testing-key issues there too).

checks/owned-paths asserts filing_steps holds 'file_issues(pending + facts + docspecs)'; filing_steps now files pending + facts + docspecs + sprints + keys, so the check fails (with t45's TESTS_SRC subprocess.run entry, also unlisted in its owned set)
tasks refile takes no --files, so a caller that must refile a task with more files makes a second write (tasks task set), which is not one state change.

stage_verify formats every fixes and promises item as 'scenario %s, round %s' from field(item, 'round'); a promise a test task records carries no round, so the verify brief says 'round None', a false detail in the brief.

tests settled, tests failures, and tests reports find a promised or verified suite defect by its test field (the failure's id: a scenario, leftovers--<kind>, schedule--<a>--<b>, or perf:<scenario>:<item>). The sprint-suite brief i07-converge adds to merge.md must copy test (and round) from the report onto the defect, or no promise ever holds a failure and no verified perf fix settles its entry.

speed_settled treats a product-slow latest verdict as settled until an accepted fixes item names it, and speed_rows passes only the run's fixes pool; certification fixes a perf entry through a verified ledger defect, so after that fix tests slowest and --stage speed never give the test the fresh speed read item 10 promises. perf_failures already counts the verified defect (this stage).

.ok-planner/review/project.md line 32: the review tool entry says checks and certified refuse a config with no lint_checks.no-tests or a testing with no runners or run, and does not say certified now reads testing.enabled and runs .ok-planner/bin/tests settled --sprint <path> --ledger <ledger> under on or frozen. Task t63 changes only the scripts/tests entry. Harm: the review loop's facts misstate certified's inputs.

scripts/tests::speed_settled settles a product-slow verdict until an accepted fixes item names it with perf=; in sprint certification the perf: fix is a defects-pool item set verified, and the ledger holds no fixes pool, so tests slowest / tests tasks --stage speed --run <ledger> keep the test settled and the fresh speed read work item 10 promises after an accepted fix happens only in the next sprint (--from state, where no carried acceptance holds). perf_failures already treats a verified defect as settling the entry; speed_settled does not read the ledger's verified defects.

median_seconds adds the ranking's carried seconds to the rounds' seconds at the same blob; running tests stamp twice for one sprint, as after a failed commit, carries this sprint's seconds into the ranking and then counts them again from the rounds. Harm: the median skews toward this sprint's values (A-class duplicate state); values are capped at testing.slowest.

scripts/review now defines SPRINTS (.ok-planner/sprints); scripts/tests keeps its own SPRINTS constant for the same path, a second copy under plumbline-coding rule 6 that could import review.SPRINTS. Also: this repo's materialized .ok-planner/bin/tests predates tests stray accepting a sprint under .ok-planner/sprints/, so review certified's stray subprocess refuses here until true-up materializes the new tests.

scripts/tests USAGE (declare, line ~73) says under testing.enabled off every run of the tool that names --sprint refuses, but testing_config refuses only where a verb reads testing for a sprint: groups, plan, run, reached, reports, settled, slowest, and tasks --stage speed; failures, stray, tasks --stage write|sweep|verify, ports, snapshot, diff, and stamp still run under off. The help text misstates the refusal set.

.claude/rules/ok-planner-cheatsheet.md:129 is the materialized copy of the family template and still says the session runs the drain as one Workflow script per drain where the harness offers one, with no owner opt-in; the next true-up rewrites it from plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ok-planner-cheatsheet.md

body: Artifact: decision test-tasks-own-the-tests, named by work item 1: 'Only the tasks of a sprint's test stages, and the test tasks sprint certification files, add, edit, or delete a test.' Code site 1: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ok-cheatsheet.md:19 (Executing a sprint), which first lists the test stages' task kinds ('support tasks, test tasks, legacy tasks, the sweep, and verify tasks') and then says 'They change no product code, and only their test tasks add, edit, or delete a test.' Code site 2: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ok-planner-CLAUDE.md:637-639: 'Where the sprint plans tests, `bin/tests tasks` files the test stages after the code stages they test, and only their test tasks add, edit, or delete a test.' What the code does instead: in both sentences 'their test tasks' reads as the one kind of test-stage task named 'test tasks', which narrows the decision's owner set (every task of a test stage) and excludes legacy tasks and the sweep. Those tasks delete tests by design: skills/converge/prompts/test-legacy.md step 2 'Then delete the test' and step 3 'Per deletion: delete the test'; skills/converge/prompts/test-sweep.md 'Otherwise delete it: git rm <file>'. The ok-cheatsheet is an always-loaded rules file in every project, so a legacy or sweep agent reads a standing rule that forbids the deletion its brief orders. The sibling texts state the decision correctly: ok-planner-CLAUDE.md:248-250 and ok-planner-cheatsheet.md:378-379 ('the tasks of its test stages, and the test tasks sprint certification files'). Scope: caused; both sentences are added by this sprint (git diff 301043a).

body: Work item 6 (test stages follow the code stages they test; B121 'takes --after'). Entry: boilerplate step 4 -> tests tasks --stage write --after <build tasks> -> scripts/tests::cmd_tasks -> stage_write(..., after). Where it ends: stage_write reuses the parameter name 'after' as a loop variable. In the scenario loop it assigns 'after = [latest_support[path] for path in support_of(plan, s) if path in latest_support]' (scripts/tests:3989), and in the blocked-on-support loop 'after = {latest_support[path] ...}' / 'after |= {...}' (4004-4005). The closing loop 'for filing in filings: if filing["op"] == "file": filing["after"] = sorted(set(filing["after"]) | set(after))' (4008-4010) then reads the last loop value, not the --after the caller gave. Trigger 1: a plan whose last written scenario names no support -> after == [] -> no test, support, or legacy task waits on the code-stage build tasks, so the test stages run beside the code stages they test, against code not yet built. Trigger 2: a plan whose last written scenario names a support file (one support file helpers/x, one new scenario using it, no existing tasks, no stack): filings are +0 (support) then +1 (test, after [+0]); the closing loop sets +0's after to ['+0'], so filed_tasks calls 'tasks file ... --after +0' for the first filing (ids has no '+0' yet), the tracker fails 'task tN waits on +0, which does not exist', tests_run raises, and --stage write files nothing and exits with an error; a later support filing can also be chained to a planned id filed after it, failing the same way. The outcome 'test stages follow the code stages' and filing the support and test tasks is not reached. Scope: caused (the base stage_write took no after parameter; it used after_controls).

Work item 6, 'The carried-over slow tests ... Its rewrites land before certification starts' (B123). Entry: boilerplate step 4 -> tests tasks --stage speed --from state -> stage_speed -> speed_candidates over live_tests (every live test in .ok-planner/test-state.json, most of them written by earlier sprints). Where it ends: the speed prompt's send-back says 'send the test back to a test task through its scenario's latest item in the tests pool ... Set the latest one for the scenario: tasks item set <item> --state sent-back' and gives no step for a scenario the pool holds no item for. A carried test no test task of this sprint wrote has no tests item in the run, so the reviewer records only the speed item. scripts/tests::refiled_tests reads only tests-pool items (sent_back_tests iterates recorded_tests(root, run)), so the next --stage write files no rewrite; stage_speed then skips the scenario (awaits_rewrite), and tests settled/unsettled_send_backs counts it settled because its test file still stands at the recorded blob. The send-back is dropped silently and the rewrite never lands. The verify prompt has the missing step ('Where it holds none, as for a kept or adopted test no test task wrote, add one: tasks item add --pool tests ... --state sent-back'); the speed prompt does not. Scope: caused (the carried-ranking speed task is new in this sprint).

Work item 6 (test stages follow the code stages) with item 11's after-list refusal. Entry: boilerplate step 4 says run --stage write '--after <the latest build task of each code stage ...>' and 'Every --stage write takes the same --after'; step 7 refiles a build that closes partial ('tasks refile <task>'), and calls every write-stage refusal a genuine blocker: 'surface its message and stop'. Path: first --stage write --after t5 files the test tasks; the drain runs; build t5 closes partial; the session refiles it as t9 (the tracker appends t9 to every open waiter); the session's next --stage write, with the same --after t5 as step 4 orders -> stage_write -> given_after_refusals (scripts/tests:3692) finds t5 'closed' with outcome 'partial' and raises '--after names build task t5 (...), which closed partial: ...; surface it as a genuine blocker'. The check never follows t5's refile chain (the refile records previous=t5), so a routine partial refile of a code stage stops the whole sprint before verify, ports, sweep, and speed run. Trigger: any code stage the test stages wait on that closes partial or blocked once and is refiled. Scope: caused (--after and given_after_refusals are new).

Work item 6, carried-over slow tests (B123): the speed reviewer must judge whether a cheaper form 'proves the same outcome' ({{TEST-SPEED-JUDGING}}). Entry: --stage speed --from state -> stage_speed. Where it ends: for a carried scenario the sprint's plan does not list, stage_speed builds the brief from 's = by_id.get(sid) or {"id": sid, "action": "keep", "text": "-"}' (scripts/tests:4364), ignoring the scenario's recorded text and source in .ok-planner/test-state.json, so scenario_brief prints 'scenario <id> (keep): -. Source: None.'; and the speed prompt's Read step 2 sends the reviewer to 'tests plan --sprint ... --show', whose print_plan lists only plan['scenarios'], so the scenario is not there either. The reviewer is never told the outcome the test proves, and judges 'same outcome' blind. Trigger: any carried slow test whose story the sprint did not re-plan, which is the common case for the carried ranking. Scope: caused (the carried-ranking speed source is new).

body: Work item 10 (product-slow): 'A product-slow verdict is never an acceptance: it settles once its fix is accepted, and the test gets a fresh speed read'; notes item 10 Calls: 'tests failures lists ... until a fix item naming it (perf=<speed item>) is accepted. The test is then unreviewed again.' Entry: tests tasks --stage speed (--round n --run <ledger>, converge SKILL Loop 2 step 2a) and tests slowest -> speed_candidates -> speed_rows -> speed_settled(items, records, fixes, ...). For a latest verdict of product-slow, speed_settled returns 'latest["id"] not in accepted_fixes(fixes)', where fixes = run_items(root, run, "fixes") (scripts/tests:4268) and accepted_fixes reads items of the 'fixes' pool carrying a 'perf' field (4187-4188). Nothing in the tree writes a 'fixes' pool item any more: the only writer at the base was the retired test sprint's fixer (git show 301043a:plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/core.md:1498, 'tasks item add --pool fixes'); rg 'pool fixes' over plugins/ finds no writer now. A perf: fix now lands as a certification ledger defect whose test is perf:<sid>:<item>, set verified by verify.md; perf_failures honors that (defect_tests(..., VERIFIED)) but speed_settled does not. Where the path ends: speed_settled returns True for every product-slow test for the rest of the sprint, so speed_candidates never picks it again and the fixed test never gets the fresh speed read the work item promises (and tests slowest omits it from the unsettled list). Scope: caused by the change (speed_settled, accepted_fixes, and the product-slow verdict are new in item 10, and item 1 retired the fixes pool's writer).

Entry A9. Trigger: sprint certification Loop 2 step 6a (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md:133) files one 'tests run --sprint <s> --only <tests>' exec task per suite defect to confirm, drains them under a cap of 8, then runs 'tests failures --json' once and confirms every defect whose test it no longer lists. Path: cmd_failures -> unsettled_failures (scripts/tests:3248-3258): 'latest = rounds[-1]; found = failing + leftover_failures(latest) + schedule_failures(latest, recorded_schedule(root))'. Since item 8, every --only --sprint run records a rerun round (B2), reruns run side by side (B3), and each round is appended at its end under results_lock with the next number (results_file), so after the drain rounds[-1] is whichever confirm run ended last, not the round of a given defect. Harm: a T2 leftovers--<kind> defect or a T4 schedule--<a>--<b> defect whose own confirm rerun grew the count again or ran a and b together again is not listed, because only the last-appended round's leftovers and schedule entries are read; step 6a then sets it verified with confirmed=<its exec task>, a confirmation that reports a fix that did not hold (and a T4 defect never goes back to rewrite). Standing test failures do not have this problem: standing_results reads every round since the latest closed whole round. The same latest-round read feeds failing_targets and tests settled. Scope: caused by the change (recorded concurrent reruns and end-of-run append are item 8's; the code follows the notes' 'the latest round's leftovers-- and schedule-- entries', but under concurrent confirm runs the latest round names no particular defect's run).

body:
Work item 7, Confirm: 'the fixed test runs again for each suite defect'. Entry: Loop 2 step 6a (skills/converge/SKILL.md:133) lists every source=suite defect that stands verified with no confirmed field and files 'tests run --sprint

--only ', 'its tests being its test field', with special cases only for leftovers-- (its tests field) and schedule---- (a and b). A T3 defect's test field is the perf entry id, 'perf::' (merge.md sprint-suite brief copies the report's test; scripts/tests::perf_failure builds it as '%s%s:%s' % (PERF_PREFIX, sid, item id)). Path: tests run --only perf:: -> scripts/tests::run_targets: 'missing = [sid for sid in args.only if sid not in live]' -> InputError 'no live test for perf:...', so the exec task fails and the scenario's test never runs. Step 6a then runs 'tests failures --json'; scripts/tests::perf_failures drops every perf entry a verified ledger defect names ('verified = defect_tests(ledger_defects(root, sprint), VERIFIED)'), so the entry is not listed and 6a sets the T3 defect 'verified --field confirmed=', naming a failed exec task as the confirmation. Where the outcome ends: the confirm never reruns the slow scenario's test after its product fix, and the ledger records a confirmation that did not happen (A9 shape). The same holds for a T3 defect at rewrite (fixer recorded the test at fault) once its test task is accepted. Scope: caused; step 6a and the T3 class are new in this sprint.

Work item 7, Find: 'Each failing test and each grown leftover count files a report', and the final whole-suite round 'repeats until a whole-suite round passes after the last change'. The notes' cross-group list for item 7 names the find source as 'tests failures (schedule--, perf:, standing failures, not run)'. Trigger: a test hangs, so the whole-suite round stops after testing.silence (or the round does not close). scripts/tests::unreported marks every target with no result 'not_run' when the run stopped, and scripts/tests::failed is 'not result["passed"] and not result.get("not_run")', so the hanging test and every test after it count as neither passed nor failed. Path: SKILL.md step 3a.1 -> 3a.2 'tests failures --json' (scripts/tests::cmd_failures -> unsettled_failures keeps only failed(standing[sid])) lists none of them, so no rerun is filed; 3a.3 'tests reports' (scripts/tests::suite_reports: 'if failed(result)') adds no report, so no defect and no fixer exists for the hang. Loop 2 step 2a then runs 'tests settled' (scripts/tests::settled_failures: '<sids> ran in no round since whole-suite round N: run the whole suite again') -> NOT SETTLED; tests failures lists nothing, no speed send-back stands, so 2a's third bullet, 'a test ran in no round since it: run this step again', reruns the whole suite, which stops at the same hang. Where it ends: the final whole-suite round loops without end, filing nothing, and certification never reaches its return (review certified stays SPRINT NOT COMPLETE). Scope: caused; the suite as a find source, settled, and step 2a are new in this sprint.

body: B205 rules that after true-up removes the vendored plan-tests, true-up's report names its replacement. The front door /ok writes that report: plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md says '<for each retired verb removed:> `<name>` is gone; <its replacement, or "retired, with no replacement">' and then 'Name each removed verb's replacement from the retired-verb table in the administration document:', followed by its own inline copy of that table (lines ~113-128). The inline copy has no plan-tests row. Only ADMINISTRATION.md:385 gained '| `plan-tests` | `/plan-sprint` plans each sprint's tests; `/ok-setup` sets testing up |'. Trigger: /ok trues up a project that vendors .claude/skills/plan-tests/; retired_payload_steps removes it (plan-tests is now in RETIRED_VENDORED). Path: admin/true-up::retired_payload_steps removes the skill -> /ok SKILL step 'for each retired verb removed' -> the inline table the session reads holds no row for plan-tests. Harm: the report the owner reads can say plan-tests is 'retired, with no replacement', or name no replacement, which is false (A9). The owner then has no pointer to /ok-setup or /plan-sprint. The B205 outcome is reached only in part. Scope: reached. The file stood the same at the base, and this change's retirement of plan-tests exposes it.

"the retired vendored file .claude/skills/%s")' for it. ADMINISTRATION.md is the document the /ok session reads to explain every plan step. body: Entry A9. config-check passes a testing config that the tests tool refuses. ADMINISTRATION.md line 227 says one definition decides whether the config is well formed: the lint's config-check. Trigger: .ok-planner/config.json testing.offers ["stale","stale"], or testing.schedule/reaches {"form":"none","said":""} or said "  ". Path: admin/true-up::parsed_config -> plumbline config-check -> configDefects -> testingDefects -> testingSettingDefects. TESTING_SETTINGS.offers only checks that each member is drawn from TESTING_OFFERS (plumbline:358 'v.every((entry) => TESTING_OFFERS.includes(entry))'), and formAndSaid accepts any string said (plumbline:352 'v.said === null || typeof v.said === "string"'). The tests tool refuses both: scripts/tests::offers_listed requires 'len(set(offers)) == len(offers)', and scripts/tests::form_and_said requires said None or is_command (non-blank). ADMINISTRATION.md 227 states offers names each kind 'at most once'. Harm: config-check exits 0, so true-up's amend/resolve accepts and writes such a draft and the plan raises no config question; then every tests verb that reads testing (offers, groups, plan, run --sprint, settled) refuses. The sibling validators (silence, named, setup, runners) agree with the tests reader; only the new ones disagree. Scope: caused (B228/B10 added these validators in this change).

R5. Changed site: scripts/plumbline::openSprintWindow (B37). Boundary: stored state, a sprint an earlier release executed and certified that still sits under .ok-planner/sprints/ with its -base.txt, awaiting the owner's archive. B37 says 'Nothing across a boundary: a test sprint still open is moved by true-up', and names no such sprint. Before (base openTestSprint): the no-tests window opened only for an uncompleted test sprint under .ok-planner/test-sprints/; an ordinary executed sprint never opened it. After: openSprintWindow opens for any sprint with .md and -base.txt and no -certified.txt (plumbline:684 'if (fs.existsSync(path.join(folder, stem + CERTIFIED_SUFFIX))) continue;'). The earlier release's review certified printed SPRINT COMPLETE and wrote no mark, and true-up writes none (rg 'certified' admin/true-up: no hits). So in a trued-up project whose testing.enabled true-up computes as on (test-state.json stamped), the no-tests check stays off for every test edit until the owner archives that certified sprint, though the carried cheatsheet rule (docs/plumbline-cheatsheet.md:138) says the window lasts only 'until .ok-planner/bin/review certified passes for that sprint'. Scope: caused.

body: B121 / work item 6: `tests tasks --stage write --after <code-stage build tasks>` does not chain the test stages behind the code stages. stage_write takes the --after list as its parameter `after`, then rebinds the same name inside the scenario loop (tests:3978 `after = [latest_support[path] for path in support_of(plan, s) if path in latest_support]`) and the blocked-test loop (tests:4011 `after = {latest_support[path] ...}`). The closing pass (tests:4014-4016 `for filing in filings: if filing["op"] == "file": filing["after"] = sorted(set(filing["after"]) | set(after))`) then adds the last loop value, not the --after list, to every new filing. Trigger: any sprint whose plan writes at least one scenario (the boilerplate's step 4 call on the sprint run). Outcomes: (a) the last written scenario has no support file: --after is dropped, so every support, test, and legacy task is ready at once and runs beside the code stages whose code it tests, which the boilerplate's step 4 and the item-6 call say must not happen; (b) the last scenario's support file gets a support task in the same call: its placeholder (e.g. "+0") is added to every new filing, the support task's own included; filed_tasks passes it unresolved (`ids.get(dep, dep)` before that filing has an id) to `tasks file --after +0`, and the tracker's check_dependencies refuses ("waits on +0, which does not exist"), so the first write stage of such a sprint fails every time and files nothing; (c) the support task exists from an earlier call: every new filing waits on that one unrelated support task, and --after is still dropped. Scope: caused by the change (the base stage_write took no --after; the shadowing came with B121).

B223 reads an absent -plan.json as a plan of no tests in every run reader (budget_workers, tested_round/recorded_round, live_tests, run_targets, stray_paths, cmd_tasks), so a sprint planned before this release (D7) runs as a sprint of no planned tests. changed_targets, the target picker of `tests run --sprint <path> --changed`, still calls read_plan (tests:3106 `current = run_blobs(root, plan_folders(read_plan(root, sprint)), ...)`), where recorded_round beside it calls sprint_plan (tests:3153). Trigger: `.ok-planner/bin/tests run --sprint .ok-planner/sprints/<a sprint with no -plan.json>.md --changed`, a verb project.md lists for developers and operators. Outcome: it refuses with `no plan at <sprint>-plan.json: assemble it with tests plan --sprint <sprint> --from-run <run>`, which tells the user to plan tests for a sprint that is already executing, where `--only` and `--failing` on the same sprint run as a plan of no tests. Expected: the project's folders and the scenario list's live tests, as sprint_plan gives. Scope: caused by the change (the verb and its read_plan call are new in this sprint); no skill step calls --changed, so it reaches only a person or agent who runs it by hand.

body: Build call i145 (t40, work item 2). A2 harm: a second /ok-setup on the same day truncates the first one's committed budget run. Trigger: the owner runs /ok-setup and budgets the stack, then runs /ok-setup again the same day to change the budget, or to retry after the budget did not hold. Path: SKILL.md 3.5 names the run by date alone, '.ok-planner/tasks/ok-setup-<date>.jsonl' (line 91), and says: 'Where tasks init refuses because an earlier /ok-setup of the same day left the run file, pass --force: the earlier run's budget is already recorded, or was never recorded' (line 100). scripts/tasks::cmd_init with --force runs open(full, "w").close() (scripts/tasks:960), which empties the earlier run's log: its budget task's close and result, its budget and limits items, and its calls pool. Those records stand behind the budget that tests budget wrote into .ok-planner/test-state.json. An earlier run the owner interrupted mid-drain is erased too. Sibling shape: every other ceremony that opens a ledger under .ok-planner/tasks/ or review/runs/ names it with a <date>T<time> stamp from date +%Y-%m-%dT%H%M%S and never reuses an existing file: triage-issues/SKILL.md:40 and converge/SKILL.md:54. Scope: caused. skills/ok-setup/ is new in this sprint.

body: R3, B13 (rewrite). User left behind: sprint certification's suite loop, skills/converge/SKILL.md steps 3a and 2a, through tests failures (unsettled_failures), tests reports (suite_reports), and tests settled (settled_failures). Its goal, from the cross-group note for item 7 ('The suite as a find source reads tests failures (schedule--, perf:, standing failures, not run)') and item 7's end check, is to turn every way a whole-suite round fails into a report a fixer can act on, and so reach a passing whole round. Trigger: a test hangs, so the suite command writes no result line and no output for testing.silence seconds and read_stream stops the round (found['stopped']='silence'). Old outcome (base tests::unreported): every unreached test, the hung one included, was recorded passed=false and counted as failed, so tests reports filed T1 reports and fixers looked at the hang. New outcome: tests:2661-2662 marks each unreached test not_run; failed() (tests:2666) excludes not_run from every reader, so unsettled_failures (tests:3255) lists none, suite_reports (tests:3353) files no report, and the stop itself is reported nowhere. The stopped round still closes (no error), so it is the latest closed whole round, and settled_failures says only '<ids> ran in no round since whole-suite round N: run the whole suite again' (tests:3433). SKILL.md:125 answers that with 'run this step again', a whole round that stops at the same hang. The suite loop has no cap for suite defects, so certification reruns the whole suite forever and no defect, report, or fixer ever names the hung test. Scope: caused by the change (B13, and the uncapped suite loop of item 7).

C2 under A3 (a developer's or operator's action through a script the project ships, tests run, gives an error that does not tell the user what they did wrong). Trigger: tests run --sprint <S> --changed, where S is an approved sprint with no -plan.json beside it (D7: sprints planned before this release, which B223 rules every run reader takes as a plan of no tests, with the project's folders and the state's kept tests live). Path: tests::main -> cmd_run -> changed_targets -> read_plan. tests:3106 reads 'current = run_blobs(root, plan_folders(read_plan(root, sprint)), ...)', and read_plan refuses 'no plan at <S>-plan.json: assemble it with tests plan --sprint <S> --from-run <run>'. Harm: the user gets told to assemble a plan for an approved sprint whose planning is over, instead of the rerun every other run reader gives it; the sibling that records the same blobs, recorded_round at tests:3153, reads the same folders through sprint_plan, which B223 made the one reading of an absent plan. --failing and a bare --sprint run work on the same sprint, so only --changed refuses. Scope: caused by the change (changed_targets is new in item 9).

body: B207/B211 rule that true-up archives an open test sprint and files one intake issue for each open test sprint. open_test_sprints() treats every .md under .ok-planner/test-sprints/ as a test sprint, leaving out only <stem>-completion.md beside <stem>.md. The base test sprint template (git show 301043a:plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/test-sprint-document.md, step 4) has the executing session write each role prompt to .ok-planner/test-sprints/<name>-<role>.md: control, preflight, support, test, legacy, sweep, fix, verify, and speed. Trigger: a project that started executing a test sprint before updating. Path: build_plan -> test_sprint_steps -> record_folder_step returns every pair, and plan['test_sprints'] keeps each pair whose src is in open_test_sprints(), so every role prompt is kept -> filing_steps -> test_sprint_issues. Old outcome: none (the base brought the test sprint current). New outcome: besides the real sprint's issue, up to nine more issues named test-sprint-left-open-<name>-<role>. Each has the title 'The test sprint .ok-planner/test-sprints/<name>-control.md was left open and is archived' and the body 'Its plan names no story', so it reports a prompt file as an open test sprint (A9). The intake gets false judgment issues that /plan-sprint must walk. ADMINISTRATION.md 'The open test sprint's issue' states the same definition. Scope: caused by the change (new code).

Where test_state_conversion()[0] is None, cleared_stories_text writes into the open test sprint's issue: 'True-up cleared no test stamp, since .ok-planner/test-state.json holds no scenario list in the earlier form.' test_state_conversion also returns None in three cases where the file does hold the earlier form: it does not decode as UTF-8, the tests tool refuses to convert it (returncode != 0), or it changed while true-up read it. Trigger: an open test sprint with a -plan.json that names stories, plus an earlier-form test-state.json that the carried tests tool refuses, for example one whose stories or scenarios it rejects. Path: build_plan -> test_sprint_steps -> filing_steps -> test_sprint_issues -> cleared_stories_text. Harm: the filed issue gives the owner a false reason why no stamp was cleared. The owner reads the stories' stamps as settled, though the scenario list was never converted and the planned stories were never cleared, as B207's ruling requires. The 'left:' note that tells the truth prints only in diagnose and is not in the issue. Scope: caused by the change (new code).

body: Scratch repo project/ with the estate trued up at project/app (true-up wrote folders ["."]) and owned code at project/shared/util.py. Declared folders [".","../shared"]: review files, review changed, review areas, review checks, the lint, and the edit hook each reached ../shared/util.py. Then declared folders [".","../shared","../nope"] (one mistyped entry beside a valid one) and changed shared/util.py. The lint refuses that config (plumbline . exit 1: 'error: .ok-planner/config.json: folders[2] "../nope" is not an existing directory'), but the review tool proceeds with a code default: review changed printed 'review: .ok-planner/config.json sets a malformed folders, so the review reads the project root alone; run /ok, which repairs it:' then only 'changed .ok-planner/config.json', exit 0, leaving out the changed ../shared/util.py that the valid entry declares; review files and review areas likewise listed only main.py and the two config files, exit 0 (areas.json files: ['.ok-planner/config.json', '.ok-planner/review/config.json', 'main.py']). With the good config the same review changed printed 'changed ../shared/util.py'. The story promises: no check the suite runs over my project misses code I own; decision project-declares-its-folders says every tool reads the one list so the lint and review do not drift, and settings-have-no-code-defaults says code that finds a setting unusable refuses rather than defaulting. Saw: one mistyped entry makes every /converge mode's file population (hunt areas, sprint changed files, review checks) silently drop every declared folder and run exit 0 on the root alone, while the lint refuses the same config; evidence quoted above.

In a scratch project (stack up --name grow-test-coverage-a-part-at-a-time-eedeaa6d, git init, true-up), seeded 12 stories, src/a.py citing gtc-s01 and gtc-s05, ran `tests declare --enabled on ... --offers untested stale legacy runtime`. `tests offers` printed untested:1 (gtc-s01, gtc-s05), untested:2 (8 stories), untested:3 (gtc-s11, gtc-s12). Sprint 1 took untested:1 through `tests groups --take untested:1`, planned one new scenario per story, `tests plan` wrote the plan, a write task recorded both tests, archived, `tests stamp` stamped; next `tests offers` dropped gtc-s01/gtc-s05 and offered the other 10 (achieved so far). Sprint 2 took the group of gtc-s11 and gtc-s12: the story planner recorded the `stories` item for gtc-s11 and, as TEST-SCENARIO-DEFINITION directs for a story whose benefit no executable code carries ("prose has no tests"), no scenario and one call of kind untested; gtc-s12 got one new scenario. `tests plan` accepted it (calls: 1), the test was written, the sprint archived, `tests stamp` printed "story stamps: gtc-s11, gtc-s12; cleared: none". The next `tests offers` printed again "untested:2: 1 untested stories / - gtc-s11: no recorded scenario". Cause: offer_groups in plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests (line ~899) counts a story untested where it has no recorded scenario and its slug is not in `{entry.get("story") for entry in state["unguarded"]}`, but the only writer of `unguarded` (plan assembly, line ~1855) records `{path, reason}` for a program answer and never a `story`, and the story test stamp, which the stamp wrote for gtc-s11, is never read for the untested kind. So a story a sprint planned, whose approved plan legitimately holds no scenario, is re-offered as untested in every later sprint. the story promises: a project with many untested stories reaches full coverage one group at a time, so no round takes it all on (decision testing-runs-inside-the-sprint: "Offers in groups let a project with many untested stories reach full coverage one group at a time"); saw: the untested offer never empties for any story whose benefit only prose carries, and each such story is re-planned for nothing each time the owner takes its group, which in a skill-heavy project is most stories; evidence: second `tests offers` output "untested:2: 1 untested stories\n  - gtc-s11: no recorded scenario" after `tests stamp` printed "story stamps: gtc-s11, gtc-s12" and test-state.json held stamps [gtc-s01, gtc-s05, gtc-s11, gtc-s12], scenarios [gtc-s01--whole, gtc-s05--whole, gtc-s12--whole], unguarded [].

Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md (Frame "Offer the test work", section 10 step 1), tests-story.md, _sprint/shared.md TEST-SCENARIO-DEFINITION, sprint-document.md archive step 4. The skill text delivers group-at-a-time taking: it shows each group of `tests offers --json` and asks once which the sprint takes, whole or none, and passes the keys to `tests groups --take`; the archive step runs `tests stamp`. Divergence is in the script the skill calls: `tests offers` (offer_groups, scripts/tests ~line 899) offers as untested every story with no recorded scenario unless an `unguarded` entry names it by a `story` field, which no writer sets (plan assembly ~line 1855 writes only {path, reason}). TEST-SCENARIO-DEFINITION says "A skill, a rule, a document, and the design corpus are prose, and prose has no tests", so a story whose benefit is only prose is planned with no scenario; after its sprint stamps it, Frame offers it again as "no recorded scenario". the story promises: "a project with many untested stories reaches full coverage without any one round of work taking it all on"; saw: in a scratch drive, gtc-s11 planned with zero scenarios and one untested call, stamped by `tests stamp` ("story stamps: gtc-s11, gtc-s12"), was offered again by the next `tests offers` as "untested:2: 1 untested stories / - gtc-s11: no recorded scenario"; evidence: as in the tests-surface failure for this story.

body: Reviewed /plan-docs (SKILL.md steps 2-7), its doc-sprint template, and scripts/docs, then ran them in a scratch project (stack run keep-documentation-current-eedeaa6d): committed tool.py --bye, planned a documentation sprint at e55fcf1 (Window line 'Planned against commit e55fcf1'), then committed tool.py --loud before execution, recorded the base per step 3, ran writer/style/checker tasks, archived, committed, and ran 'docs stamp'. The story promises: after each update a reader finds documentation that describes the product as it stands. Saw: nothing compares the run's base with the planned commit. Step 3 of the template only says 'Where git status --porcelain lists a path outside .ok-planner/, name those paths to the owner and stop. Otherwise write the output of git rev-parse HEAD to the file beside this one', and 'docs stamp' (cmd_stamp) sets state['stamp'] = args.commit for every planned docspec. So a product change committed between the plan and its execution, which no planner saw and no item carries, is stamped over: the next window reports the docspec current. Evidence: after the stamp, 'docs window' printed 'docspec:guide stamp: 4bdee14e... status: current' and 'docspec:faq stamp: 4bdee14e... status: current', while 'grep -c loud docs/guide.md docs/faq.md' printed 0 for a tool that now takes --loud. The update hides the gap from every later run.

In a scratch project, ran a documentation sprint with a 'check' item (docs/faq.md under docspec faq) as the template's steps 5-8 order it: no writer and no style task for the check item (step 6 keeps the style pass 'to the files the write and change items name'), a checker recorded one claim false, step 7's fix loop filed 'tasks file --role fix --prompt write ... --key faq:docs/faq.md:1', the fixer edited and staged docs/faq.md, and a recheck held. The story promises a way to bring every document up to date whenever the owner chooses, which the template delivers as a self-sufficient unattended run. Saw: the run's own steps do not reach its contract. Contract item 1 says 'every file the run changed that still exists has a style task, except the file of a drop item', and no step files a style task for a check-item file a fixer changed after the style pass. Evidence: 'docs complete --sprint .ok-planner/doc-sprints/2026-11-07-guide.md' printed 'DOCS NOT COMPLETE ... - docspec:faq:  changed in this run and has no style task' with exit 2; it printed DOCS COMPLETE only after I filed an extra style task (key faq:docs/faq.md) that no step names. Step 8's 'work each failure it names' recovers it, but the steps and the contract disagree.

body: Reviewed the execution boilerplate a sprint carries (plan-sprint/sprint-document.md steps 3-4), the plan-sprint test planning step 1 (SKILL.md), and tests cmd_tasks/stage_speed. The build-stage speed read runs only inside the test stages, and the test stages open only where a -plan.json stands: step 3 says 'Where <sprint-name>-plan.json stands beside this file, the sprint plans tests, and the run opens its test stages too' (and only then registers the speed prompt), and step 4's speed step ('Then, where .ok-planner/bin/tests enabled prints on, run tests tasks ... --stage speed --from state once') sits under 'Where the run opened test stages'. plan-sprint SKILL.md test planning step 1 writes no plan where tests groups prints 'nothing to plan' ('the sprint plans no tests: write the ## Tests section with ... Plan: none: nothing to plan'). So under testing.enabled on, every sprint whose work touches no tested story and whose owner takes no offer group runs no speed read in its build stages, however many slow unaccepted tests the suite holds; the stage_speed verb itself would also refuse there for the unregistered speed prompt. The story promises: the suite is sped up as part of the work the owner already runs, so a full run takes less time over the project's life. Decision tests-spend-time-only-on-their-outcome: 'In the build stages. Under testing.enabled on, a speed task reads the testing.slowest slowest tests of the last whole-suite run that hold no speed acceptance at their current test file. Their rewrites land before sprint certification starts.' (no condition on the sprint planning tests). Saw: the build-stage speed read is skipped for every no-plan sprint.

Reviewed the archive steps of the sprint boilerplate (plan-sprint/sprint-document.md archive step 4), converge SKILL.md step 3a/2a, and tests cmd_stamp/run_targets/live_tests. A sprint with no -plan.json still runs the whole recorded suite in certification: tests run --sprint takes live_tests(root, sprint), every scenario the scenario list records, and records each test's seconds in the sprint's -results.jsonl; under on, a failed 2a round also files speed tasks and lands rewrites and speed acceptances in the certification ledger. But the stamp that carries those seconds and acceptances forward runs only 'Where <sprint-name>-plan.json stands beside the archived sprint, run .ok-planner/bin/tests stamp ...', and cmd_stamp calls read_plan, which refuses 'no plan at ...' with no -plan.json. So a no-plan sprint's whole-suite seconds never reach test-state.json's ranking and its speed acceptances are never stamped: the next sprint's --from state ranking stays at the older rounds, and a test a reader accepted in that sprint is read again. The story promises: the suite gets faster over the sprints the owner already runs. Decision tests-spend-time-only-on-their-outcome: 'A passing whole-suite round ends a sprint's speed work, and its seconds feed the next sprint's ranking.' and 'A speed acceptance ... holds across sprints until the test's own file changes'. Saw: for a sprint with nothing to plan, neither feeds forward.

Reviewed converge SKILL.md sprint mode: step 3a (the suite) runs the first whole-suite round, then 'Each failing test alone' and 'The reports', and goes to the drive and the merge; no speed step follows it. The speed step appears only in Loop 2 step 2a: 'Where .ok-planner/bin/tests failures ... lists a failure, the round failed. Where the testing state is on, run the speed step first: .ok-planner/bin/tests tasks ... --stage speed --run <this run's ledger> --round <the round's number>'. So when certification's first whole-suite round (3a) fails, the fix loop runs and the next whole-suite round (2a) runs with no speed read of the failed round's slowest tests; if that 2a round passes, the certification ends with no speed work at all despite a failed round. The story promises: the suite is sped up as part of the work the owner already runs. Decision tests-spend-time-only-on-their-outcome: 'After a failed whole-suite round. Before the next round runs, a speed task reads the testing.slowest slowest tests of the failed round that hold no speed acceptance at their current test file. Their rewrites run in the round that must run anyway.' Saw: the first failed round, the most common failed round, gets no speed read before the next round runs.

No step lists the run's calls (no 'tasks calls', no render), and /ok-setup has no completion report, so nothing asks the owner which call to veto or files a vetoed one. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md:Loop 2 step 6a. What it does: for every verified suite defect with no confirmed field it files 'tests run --sprint

--only ', 'its tests being its test field', with special cases only for leftovers-- and schedule----. A T3 defect's test field is the perf entry id 'perf::' (prompts/merge.md sprint-suite add copies the report's test; scripts/tests::perf_failure builds '%s%s:%s' % (PERF_PREFIX, sid, item['id'])). Trigger: a T3 (product slow) defect reaches verified. Path: tests run --only perf:: -> scripts/tests::run_targets:2865 'missing = [sid for sid in args.only if sid not in live]' -> InputError 'no live test for perf:...', so the exec task fails and no test runs; then 'tests failures --json' omits the entry because scripts/tests::perf_failures drops every perf entry a verified ledger defect names ('verified = defect_tests(ledger_defects(root, sprint), VERIFIED)'), so 6a sets the defect 'verified --field confirmed=', naming a failed exec task as the confirmation. Harm (C1, work item 7's 'the fixed test runs again for each suite defect'): the slow scenario's test never reruns after its product fix, and the ledger records a confirmation that did not happen. Scope: caused; step 6a and the T3 class are new in this sprint (base SKILL.md has no step 6a). Reports: i32.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:suite_reports (with unsettled_failures, settled_failures, and skills/converge/SKILL.md Loop 2 step 2a). What it does: when a test hangs, read_stream stops the whole-suite round after testing.silence (found['stopped']='silence'); recorded_round still closes the round; tests::unreported:2661 marks the hung test and every unreached test not_run, and tests::failed:2667 'not result["passed"] and not result.get("not_run")' excludes them. So unsettled_failures lists none (tests failures files no rerun), suite_reports ('if failed(result)') adds no report, and the stop itself is reported nowhere. settled_failures:3431 then prints '<sids> ran in no round since whole-suite round N: run the whole suite again', and SKILL.md step 2a's last bullet answers 'run this step again', a whole round that stops at the same hang. Trigger: any test that hangs in sprint certification's suite. In a scratch project (stack up --name grow-test-coverage-a-part-at-a-time-eedeaa6d, git init, true-up), seeded 12 stories, src/a.py citing gtc-s01 and gtc-s05, ran `tests declare --enabled on ... --offers untested stale legacy runtime`. `tests offers` printed untested:1 (gtc-s01, gtc-s05), untested:2 (8 stories), untested:3 (gtc-s11, gtc-s12). Sprint 1 took untested:1 through `tests groups --take untested:1`, planned one new scenario per story, `tests plan` wrote the plan, a write task recorded both tests, archived, `tests stamp` stamped; next `tests offers` dropped gtc-s01/gtc-s05 and offered the other 10 (achieved so far). Sprint 2 took the group of gtc-s11 and gtc-s12: the story planner recorded the `stories` item for gtc-s11 and, as TEST-SCENARIO-DEFINITION directs for a story whose benefit no executable code carries ("prose has no tests"), no scenario and one call of kind untested; gtc-s12 got one new scenario. `tests plan` accepted it (calls: 1), the test was written, the sprint archived, `tests stamp` printed "story stamps: gtc-s11, gtc-s12; cleared: none". Work item 7, Find: 'Each failing test and each grown leftover count files a report', and the final whole-suite round 'repeats until a whole-suite round passes after the last change'. The notes' cross-group list for item 7 names the find source as 'tests failures (schedule--, perf:, standing failures, not run)'. Trigger: a test hangs, so the whole-suite round stops after testing.silence (or the round does not close). scripts/tests::unreported marks every target with no result 'not_run' when the run stopped, and scripts/tests::failed is 'not result["passed"] and not result.get("not_run")', so the hanging test and every test after it count as neither passed nor failed. Loop 2 step 2a then runs 'tests settled' (scripts/tests::settled_failures: '<sids> ran in no round since whole-suite round N: run the whole suite again') -> NOT SETTLED; tests failures lists nothing, no speed send-back stands, so 2a's third bullet, 'a test ran in no round since it: run this step again', reruns the whole suite, which stops at the same hang. Where it ends: the final whole-suite round loops without end, filing nothing, and certification never reaches its return (review certified stays SPRINT NOT COMPLETE). Scope: caused; the suite as a find source, settled, and step 2a are new in this sprint.

B121 / work item 6: `tests tasks --stage write --after <code-stage build tasks>` does not chain the test stages behind the code stages. stage_write takes the --after list as its parameter `after`, then rebinds the same name inside the scenario loop (tests:3978 `after = [latest_support[path] for path in support_of(plan, s) if path in latest_support]`) and the blocked-test loop (tests:4011 `after = {latest_support[path] ...}`). The closing pass (tests:4014-4016 `for filing in filings: if filing["op"] == "file": filing["after"] = sorted(set(filing["after"]) | set(after))`) then adds the last loop value, not the --after list, to every new filing. Trigger: any sprint whose plan writes at least one scenario (the boilerplate's step 4 call on the sprint run). Outcomes: (a) the last written scenario has no support file: --after is dropped, so every support, test, and legacy task is ready at once and runs beside the code stages whose code it tests, which the boilerplate's step 4 and the item-6 call say must not happen; (b) the last scenario's support file gets a support task in the same call: its placeholder (e.g. "+0") is added to every new filing, the support task's own included; filed_tasks passes it unresolved (`ids.get(dep, dep)` before that filing has an id) to `tasks file --after +0`, and the tracker's check_dependencies refuses ("waits on +0, which does not exist"), so the first write stage of such a sprint fails every time and files nothing; (c) the support task exists from an earlier call: every new filing waits on that one unrelated support task, and --after is still dropped. Scope: caused by the change (the base stage_write took no --after; the shadowing came with B121).

B223 reads an absent -plan.json as a plan of no tests in every run reader (budget_workers, tested_round/recorded_round, live_tests, run_targets, stray_paths, cmd_tasks), so a sprint planned before this release (D7) runs as a sprint of no planned tests. changed_targets, the target picker of `tests run --sprint <path> --changed`, still calls read_plan (tests:3106 `current = run_blobs(root, plan_folders(read_plan(root, sprint)), ...)`), where recorded_round beside it calls sprint_plan (tests:3153). Trigger: `.ok-planner/bin/tests run --sprint .ok-planner/sprints/<a sprint with no -plan.json>.md --changed`, a verb project.md lists for developers and operators. Outcome: it refuses with `no plan at <sprint>-plan.json: assemble it with tests plan --sprint <sprint> --from-run <run>`, which tells the user to plan tests for a sprint that is already executing, where `--only` and `--failing` on the same sprint run as a plan of no tests. Expected: the project's folders and the scenario list's live tests, as sprint_plan gives. Scope: caused by the change (the verb and its read_plan call are new in this sprint); no skill step calls --changed, so it reaches only a person or agent who runs it by hand.

R3, B13 (rewrite). User left behind: sprint certification's suite loop, skills/converge/SKILL.md steps 3a and 2a, through tests failures (unsettled_failures), tests reports (suite_reports), and tests settled (settled_failures). Its goal, from the cross-group note for item 7 ('The suite as a find source reads tests failures (schedule--, perf:, standing failures, not run)') and item 7's end check, is to turn every way a whole-suite round fails into a report a fixer can act on, and so reach a passing whole round. Trigger: a test hangs, so the suite command writes no result line and no output for testing.silence seconds and read_stream stops the round (found['stopped']='silence'). Old outcome (base tests::unreported): every unreached test, the hung one included, was recorded passed=false and counted as failed, so tests reports filed T1 reports and fixers looked at the hang. New outcome: tests:2661-2662 marks each unreached test not_run; failed() (tests:2666) excludes not_run from every reader, so unsettled_failures (tests:3255) lists none, suite_reports (tests:3353) files no report, and the stop itself is reported nowhere. The stopped round still closes (no error), so it is the latest closed whole round, and settled_failures says only '<ids> ran in no round since whole-suite round N: run the whole suite again' (tests:3433). SKILL.md:125 answers that with 'run this step again', a whole round that stops at the same hang. The suite loop has no cap for suite defects, so certification reruns the whole suite forever and no defect, report, or fixer ever names the hung test. Scope: caused by the change (B13, and the uncapped suite loop of item 7).

C2 under A3 (a developer's or operator's action through a script the project ships, tests run, gives an error that does not tell the user what they did wrong). Trigger: tests run --sprint <S> --changed, where S is an approved sprint with no -plan.json beside it (D7: sprints planned before this release, which B223 rules every run reader takes as a plan of no tests, with the project's folders and the state's kept tests live). Path: tests::main -> cmd_run -> changed_targets -> read_plan. tests:3106 reads 'current = run_blobs(root, plan_folders(read_plan(root, sprint)), ...)', and read_plan refuses 'no plan at <S>-plan.json: assemble it with tests plan --sprint <S> --from-run <run>'. Harm: the user gets told to assemble a plan for an approved sprint whose planning is over, instead of the rerun every other run reader gives it; the sibling that records the same blobs, recorded_round at tests:3153, reads the same folders through sprint_plan, which B223 made the one reading of an absent plan. --failing and a bare --sprint run work on the same sprint, so only --changed refuses. Scope: caused by the change (changed_targets is new in item 9).

B205 rules that after true-up removes the vendored plan-tests, true-up's report names its replacement. The front door /ok writes that report: plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md says '<for each retired verb removed:> `<name>` is gone; <its replacement, or "retired, with no replacement">' and then 'Name each removed verb's replacement from the retired-verb table in the administration document:', followed by its own inline copy of that table (lines ~113-128). The inline copy has no plan-tests row. Only ADMINISTRATION.md:385 gained '| `plan-tests` | `/plan-sprint` plans each sprint's tests; `/ok-setup` sets testing up |'. Trigger: /ok trues up a project that vendors .claude/skills/plan-tests/; retired_payload_steps removes it (plan-tests is now in RETIRED_VENDORED). Path: admin/true-up::retired_payload_steps removes the skill -> /ok SKILL step 'for each retired verb removed' -> the inline table the session reads holds no row for plan-tests. Harm: the report the owner reads can say plan-tests is 'retired, with no replacement', or name no replacement, which is false (A9). The owner then has no pointer to /ok-setup or /plan-sprint. The B205 outcome is reached only in part. Scope: reached. The file stood the same at the base, and this change's retirement of plan-tests exposes it.

Item 17's notes say true-up removes the stamped .claude/skills/converge/prompts/backout.md from every project, beside RETIRED_SHARED's removals. The code does this: admin/true-up renames RETIRED_SHARED to RETIRED_SKILL_FILES and adds 'converge/prompts/backout.md', and retired_payload_steps plans 'removal(... "the retired vendored file .claude/skills/%s")' for it. ADMINISTRATION.md is the document the /ok session reads to explain every plan step. Its 'What each kind of content becomes' row (line 123) still reads '| a retired shared file (`_shared/certification-core.md`, `_shared/sprint-document.md`, `_shared/implementation-auditor.md`) or a retired agent profile ... carrying the suite stamp | remove it |'. No other part of the document names backout.md as a file true-up removes. Trigger: a project vendors the v30 converge skill and /ok trues it up. The plan then lists a removal of .claude/skills/converge/prompts/backout.md that the administration document does not describe, so the item 17 bullet ('admin/true-up and admin/ADMINISTRATION.md' covering every step) is reached only in part. Scope: caused. The sprint added the removal and left the document's list of removed files as it was.

body: Entry A9. config-check passes a testing config that the tests tool refuses. ADMINISTRATION.md line 227 says one definition decides whether the config is well formed: the lint's config-check. Trigger: .ok-planner/config.json testing.offers ["stale","stale"], or testing.schedule/reaches {"form":"none","said":""} or said "  ". Path: admin/true-up::parsed_config -> plumbline config-check -> configDefects -> testingDefects -> testingSettingDefects. TESTING_SETTINGS.offers only checks that each member is drawn from TESTING_OFFERS (plumbline:358 'v.every((entry) => TESTING_OFFERS.includes(entry))'), and formAndSaid accepts any string said (plumbline:352 'v.said === null || typeof v.said === "string"'). The tests tool refuses both: scripts/tests::offers_listed requires 'len(set(offers)) == len(offers)', and scripts/tests::form_and_said requires said None or is_command (non-blank). ADMINISTRATION.md 227 states offers names each kind 'at most once'. Harm: config-check exits 0, so true-up's amend/resolve accepts and writes such a draft and the plan raises no config question; then every tests verb that reads testing (offers, groups, plan, run --sprint, settled) refuses. The sibling validators (silence, named, setup, runners) agree with the tests reader; only the new ones disagree. Scope: caused (B228/B10 added these validators in this change).

R5. Changed site: scripts/plumbline::openSprintWindow (B37). Boundary: stored state, a sprint an earlier release executed and certified that still sits under .ok-planner/sprints/ with its -base.txt, awaiting the owner's archive. B37 says 'Nothing across a boundary: a test sprint still open is moved by true-up', and names no such sprint. Before (base openTestSprint): the no-tests window opened only for an uncompleted test sprint under .ok-planner/test-sprints/; an ordinary executed sprint never opened it. After: openSprintWindow opens for any sprint with .md and -base.txt and no -certified.txt (plumbline:684 'if (fs.existsSync(path.join(folder, stem + CERTIFIED_SUFFIX))) continue;'). The earlier release's review certified printed SPRINT COMPLETE and wrote no mark, and true-up writes none (rg 'certified' admin/true-up: no hits). So in a trued-up project whose testing.enabled true-up computes as on (test-state.json stamped), the no-tests check stays off for every test edit until the owner archives that certified sprint, though the carried cheatsheet rule (docs/plumbline-cheatsheet.md:138) says the window lasts only 'until .ok-planner/bin/review certified passes for that sprint'. Scope: caused.

B109 (rewrite): scripts/review::project_runners now returns the built-in runners where testing holds no run key (review:455, 'if "testing" not in config or (isinstance(testing, dict) and "run" not in testing): return runners'), so review checks and review certified pass a testing object such as {"enabled": "off"} with no runners and no run. User left behind: .ok-planner/review/project.md's scripts/tasks-and-review entry, the review facts every review prompt pastes in, whose own rule says a sprint build that changes a script input updates it in the same stage. It still says 'checks and certified also refuse one that sets no lint_checks.no-tests, or a testing that sets no runners or no run' (the sentence stands the same at base 301043a), and says checks refuses a check that starts 'a testing.runners command, or the words of testing.run', which now holds only where testing.run is set; it also names no refusal for a missing testing.enabled, which review certified now raises through testing_enabled. Goal and source: the facts file's header ('It holds the facts a general loop cannot know'; drivers judge A3 refusals against it). What it gets now: a driver checking review checks against a testing with no run expects a refusal, sees a pass, and reports a false defect, or trusts a refusal the tool no longer makes. Scope: caused by the change (B109 and item 2's testing_enabled).

Build call i145 (t40, work item 2). A2 harm: a second /ok-setup on the same day truncates the first one's committed budget run. Trigger: the owner runs /ok-setup and budgets the stack, then runs /ok-setup again the same day to change the budget, or to retry after the budget did not hold. Path: SKILL.md 3.5 names the run by date alone, '.ok-planner/tasks/ok-setup-<date>.jsonl' (line 91), and says: 'Where tasks init refuses because an earlier /ok-setup of the same day left the run file, pass --force: the earlier run's budget is already recorded, or was never recorded' (line 100). scripts/tasks::cmd_init with --force runs open(full, "w").close() (scripts/tasks:960), which empties the earlier run's log: its budget task's close and result, its budget and limits items, and its calls pool. Those records stand behind the budget that tests budget wrote into .ok-planner/test-state.json. An earlier run the owner interrupted mid-drain is erased too. Sibling shape: every other ceremony that opens a ledger under .ok-planner/tasks/ or review/runs/ names it with a <date>T<time> stamp from date +%Y-%m-%dT%H%M%S and never reuses an existing file: triage-issues/SKILL.md:40 and converge/SKILL.md:54. Scope: caused. skills/ok-setup/ is new in this sprint.

B207/B211 rule that true-up archives an open test sprint and files one intake issue for each open test sprint. open_test_sprints() treats every .md under .ok-planner/test-sprints/ as a test sprint, leaving out only <stem>-completion.md beside <stem>.md. The base test sprint template (git show 301043a:plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/test-sprint-document.md, step 4) has the executing session write each role prompt to .ok-planner/test-sprints/<name>-<role>.md: control, preflight, support, test, legacy, sweep, fix, verify, and speed. Trigger: a project that started executing a test sprint before updating. Path: build_plan -> test_sprint_steps -> record_folder_step returns every pair, and plan['test_sprints'] keeps each pair whose src is in open_test_sprints(), so every role prompt is kept -> filing_steps -> test_sprint_issues. Old outcome: none (the base brought the test sprint current). New outcome: besides the real sprint's issue, up to nine more issues named test-sprint-left-open-<name>-<role>. Each has the title 'The test sprint .ok-planner/test-sprints/<name>-control.md was left open and is archived' and the body 'Its plan names no story', so it reports a prompt file as an open test sprint (A9). The intake gets false judgment issues that /plan-sprint must walk. ADMINISTRATION.md 'The open test sprint's issue' states the same definition. Scope: caused by the change (new code).

Where test_state_conversion()[0] is None, cleared_stories_text writes into the open test sprint's issue: 'True-up cleared no test stamp, since .ok-planner/test-state.json holds no scenario list in the earlier form.' test_state_conversion also returns None in three cases where the file does hold the earlier form: it does not decode as UTF-8, the tests tool refuses to convert it (returncode != 0), or it changed while true-up read it. Trigger: an open test sprint with a -plan.json that names stories, plus an earlier-form test-state.json that the carried tests tool refuses, for example one whose stories or scenarios it rejects. Path: build_plan -> test_sprint_steps -> filing_steps -> test_sprint_issues -> cleared_stories_text. Harm: the filed issue gives the owner a false reason why no stamp was cleared. The owner reads the stories' stamps as settled, though the scenario list was never converted and the planned stories were never cleared, as B207's ruling requires. The 'left:' note that tells the truth prints only in diagnose and is not in the issue. Scope: caused by the change (new code).

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:speed_settled. What it does: for a latest speed verdict of product-slow it returns 'latest["id"] not in accepted_fixes(fixes)', and speed_rows passes fixes = run_items(root, run, "fixes") (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:4268); accepted_fixes reads accepted 'fixes' pool items carrying 'perf' (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:4187-4188). Nothing in the tree writes a 'fixes' pool item now: a perf: fix lands as a certification ledger defect whose test is perf:<sid>:<item>, set verified; perf_failures honors that (defect_tests(ledger_defects(root, sprint), VERIFIED), plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:4240) but speed_settled does not. Trigger: a speed reviewer records product-slow and certification verifies the perf: fix. Harm (C1, work item 10: 'it settles once its fix is accepted, and the test gets a fresh speed read'): speed_settled stays True for that test for the rest of the sprint, so tests slowest and --stage speed never give the fixed test its fresh speed read. Reports: i16, i18.

.ok-planner/review/project.md, the scripts/tasks-and-review entry. What it says of certified: 'checks and certified also refuse one that sets no lint_checks.no-tests, or a testing that sets no runners or no run', and nothing of certified's testing inputs. What the code does now (B125, work item 7): scripts/review::cmd_certified reads testing.enabled through testing_enabled (review:442-445, refusing a missing or malformed value) and, under on or frozen, runs tests settled --sprint <path> --ledger <ledger> through suite_failures (review:2095-2097). Trigger: a review agent or driver that judges review certified against the pasted facts. Harm (A9): the review facts every review prompt pastes in misstate certified's inputs and refusals, so a driver reports a false defect or misses a real one. Report: i17.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:median_seconds, with cmd_stamp. What it does: values = the ranking's carried seconds at the blob (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:2721-2722) plus every passing result of the sprint's closed whole rounds at the same blob (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:2723-2729); cmd_stamp writes speed_ranking's values back into test-state.json's ranking (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:4649-4655). Trigger: tests stamp runs twice for one archived sprint, as when the archive step's commit fails and the step runs again. Harm (A7, accepted data doubled): the second stamp counts this sprint's seconds once from the ranking the first stamp wrote and again from the same rounds, so the stored ranking holds them twice and the median skews toward them. Report: i19.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:SPRINTS. What it does: scripts/tests defines SPRINTS = os.path.join(ESTATE, "sprints") (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:534), while scripts/review, which tests loads and whose review.ARCHIVED_SPRINTS it uses beside it (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:1136-1137), defines SPRINTS = os.path.join(".ok-planner", "sprints") (review:68). Neither constant stood at base 301043a. Harm (A8, plumbline-coding rule 6, 'Import, never copy'): two copies of one path the change added. Report: i20; its note that the materialized .ok-planner/bin/tests lags is the dogfood copy the next /ok rewrites, not a defect of this tree.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:USAGE, the declare entry. What it says: 'under off, every run of this tool that names --sprint refuses, and a run without --sprint still runs'. What the code does: testing_config refuses under off only for the verbs that read testing for a sprint (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:728-733); cmd_failures (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:3294) and cmd_stray (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:3556) never call it, nor do tasks --stage write|verify|sweep, snapshot, and diff, and each runs under off. Trigger: a developer reads tests --help with testing.enabled off. Harm (A9): the help text says those verbs refuse under off, which is false. Report: i21.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ok-cheatsheet.md:19 ('Executing a sprint') and scripts/ok-planner-CLAUDE.md:637-639. What they say: after listing the test stages' tasks (support tasks, test tasks, legacy tasks, the sweep, and verify tasks), 'only their test tasks add, edit, or delete a test'. Commitment: decision test-tasks-own-the-tests, named by work item 1: 'Only the tasks of a sprint's test stages, and the test tasks sprint certification files, add, edit, or delete a test.' Harm (C4): the always-loaded rule narrows the owner set to the one task kind 'test tasks' and forbids the deletions the legacy and sweep briefs order (skills/converge/prompts/test-legacy.md:24 'Per deletion: delete the test'; test-sweep.md:20 'Otherwise delete it: git rm <file>'). The sibling ok-planner-CLAUDE.md:248-250 states the decision as written. The sprint added both sentences. Report: i24.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:cmd_groups, with skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md section 10 step 1. What it does: cmd_groups prints 'nothing to plan' where 'not touched and not sort and not record["runtime"]' (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:1596), ignoring the run's answered program questions, and SKILL.md then writes 'Plan: none: nothing to plan', so no tests plan runs and no -plan.json is written. The only path that carries a no-guard answer into test-state.json is assembled_plan (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:1841-1856, plan['unguarded']) -> -plan.json -> cmd_stamp (state.update(unguarded=plan['unguarded'])), and the archive step stamps only where -plan.json stands. Trigger: testing on or frozen, a sprint whose work items name a program no story serves, no offer taken and no tested story re-planned; the owner answers the program question 'no guard'. Harm (C1, work item 3 and SKILL.md's programs step: 'no guard, with the reason, so later plans do not ask again'): the answer lives only in the planning run; tests-programs.md reads only the scenario list's unguarded list, so the next /plan-sprint asks the owner the same question again. Report: i25.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_write. What it does: it takes the --after list as its parameter 'after', then rebinds the name in the scenario loop ('after = [latest_support[path] for path in support_of(plan, s) if path in latest_support]', plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:3978) and the blocked-on-support loop ('after = {latest_support[path] ...}' / 'after |= {...}', plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:4011-4012); the closing pass ('filing["after"] = sorted(set(filing["after"]) | set(after))', plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:4014-4016) adds the last loop value, not the caller's --after. Trigger: boilerplate step 4's --stage write --after <build tasks> on a plan that writes a scenario. Harm (C1, work item 6 / B121, test stages follow the code stages they test): where the last scenario names no support, --after is dropped and the test tasks run beside the code stages they test; where it names a support file planned in the same call, the placeholder '+0' joins every filing, the tracker refuses 'waits on +0, which does not exist', and the write stage files nothing. Report: i26.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/test-speed.md, the Send back record. What it says: 'send the test back to a test task through its scenario's latest item in the tests pool ... Set the latest one for the scenario: tasks item set <item> --state sent-back', with no step where the pool holds no item for the scenario. A carried test from the ranking in test-state.json (--stage speed --from state) that no test task of this sprint wrote has no tests item in the run; plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:refiled_tests reads only tests-pool items (sent_back_tests over recorded_tests, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:3784-3812), so no rewrite is filed; stage_speed then skips the scenario (awaits_rewrite) and tests settled counts it settled while the file stands at its blob. The verify prompt has the missing step (test-verify.md:128-131, 'Where it holds none, as for a kept or adopted test no test task wrote, add one'). Trigger: the build-stage speed reviewer sends back a carried test. Harm (C1, work item 6: 'Its rewrites land before certification starts'): the send-back is dropped silently and the rewrite never lands. Report: i27.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:given_after_refusals, with sprint-document.md boilerplate steps 4 and 7. What it does: for each --after task closed other than done it refuses 'which closed partial ...; surface it as a genuine blocker' (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:3692-3705), never following the task's refile chain. Step 4 says 'Every --stage write takes the same --after'; step 7 refiles a build that closes partial with tasks refile, and calls every write-stage refusal a genuine blocker: 'surface its message and stop'. Trigger: a code stage the test stages wait on closes partial or blocked once and is refiled; the session's next --stage write passes the same --after. Harm (C1, work item 6 with item 11's after-list refusal): a routine refile of a code stage stops the sprint before verify, ports, sweep, and speed run. Report: i28.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_speed. What it does: for a carried scenario the sprint's plan does not list, it builds the brief from 's = by_id.get(sid) or {"id": sid, "action": "keep", "text": "-"}' (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:4364), ignoring the scenario's recorded text and source in test-state.json (live entries carry only PLAN_TEXT reach, entry, waits, kind, setup, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:590), so scenario_brief prints 'scenario <id> (keep): -. Source: None.'; the speed prompt's Read step 2 points at tests plan --show, which lists only the plan's scenarios. Trigger: any carried slow test whose story the sprint did not re-plan. Harm (C1, work item 6 / B123 with {{TEST-SPEED-JUDGING}}): the reviewer is never told the outcome the test proves and judges whether a cheaper form 'proves the same outcome' blind. Report: i29.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:speed_settled. Same flaw as the sprint-noticed defect: a product-slow latest verdict settles while 'latest["id"] not in accepted_fixes(fixes)', fixes being the run's 'fixes' pool (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:4268, 4187-4188), which nothing writes now; a perf: fix lands as a verified certification ledger defect, which perf_failures reads and speed_settled does not. Harm (C1, work item 10: 'it settles once its fix is accepted, and the test gets a fresh speed read'): speed_candidates never picks the fixed test again and tests slowest omits it. Report: i30.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:unsettled_failures. What it does: 'latest = rounds[-1]; found = failing + leftover_failures(latest) + schedule_failures(latest, recorded_schedule(root))' (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:3256-3257), reading leftovers-- and schedule-- entries from the last-appended round only. Since item 8 every --only --sprint run records a rerun round, reruns run side by side, and each appends at its end. Trigger: converge SKILL.md Loop 2 step 6a files one tests run --only exec per suite defect, drains them under a cap of 8, then runs tests failures --json once. Harm (A9): a T2 leftovers--<kind> or T4 schedule--<a>--<b> defect whose own confirm rerun grew the count or ran a and b together again is not listed when another confirm run ended later, so step 6a sets it verified with confirmed=<its exec task>, a confirmation of a fix that did not hold. Report: i31.

Set the latest one for the scenario: tasks item set <item> --state sent-back', with no step where the pool holds no item for the scenario.
