Harm (C1, work item 6 / B123 with {{TEST-SPEED-JUDGING}}): the reviewer is never told the outcome the test proves and judges whether a cheaper form 'proves the same outcome' blind. Report: i29.

brief:
fix round 1; defects i82 i91
- i82: .ok-planner/review/project.md:Scripts for developers and operators, the scripts/tasks-and-review entry (B109, rewrite). What it does: says 'checks and certified also refuse one that sets no lint_checks.no-tests, or a testing that sets no runners or no run' and that checks refuses a check that starts 'a testing.runners command, or the words of testing.run' unconditionally; the sentence stands as at base 301043a. The change made scripts/review::project_runners return the built-in runners where testing holds no run key (review:456 'if "testing" not in config or (isinstance(testing, dict) and "run" not in testing): return runners'), so review checks and review certified pass a testing such as {"enabled": "off"} with no runners and no run; and review certified now refuses a missing testing.enabled through testing_enabled, which the entry does not name. User left behind (R3): the review facts file every review prompt pastes in, whose own header says a sprint build that changes a script input updates it in the same stage. Harm: a driver judging review checks against a testing with no run expects a refusal, sees a pass, and reports a false defect, or trusts a refusal the tool no longer makes. Scope: caused (B109 and item 2's testing_enabled). Reports: i43.

--only ', 'its tests being its test field', with special cases only for leftovers-- and schedule----. A T3 defect's test field is the perf entry id 'perf::' (prompts/merge.md sprint-suite add copies the report's test; scripts/tests::perf_failure builds '%s%s:%s' % (PERF_PREFIX, sid, item['id'])). Trigger: a T3 (product slow) defect reaches verified. Path: tests run --only perf:: -> scripts/tests::run_targets:2865 'missing = [sid for sid in args.only if sid not in live]' -> InputError 'no live test for perf:...', so the exec task fails and no test runs; then 'tests failures --json' omits the entry because scripts/tests::perf_failures drops every perf entry a verified ledger defect names ('verified = defect_tests(ledger_defects(root, sprint), VERIFIED)'), so 6a sets the defect 'verified --field confirmed=', naming a failed exec task as the confirmation. Harm (C1, work item 7's 'the fixed test runs again for each suite defect'): the slow scenario's test never reruns after its product fix, and the ledger records a confirmation that did not happen. Scope: caused; step 6a and the T3 class are new in this sprint (base SKILL.md has no step 6a). Reports: i32. - i64: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:suite_reports (with unsettled_failures, settled_failures, and skills/converge/SKILL.md Loop 2 step 2a). What it does: when a test hangs, read_stream stops the whole-suite round after testing.silence (found['stopped']='silence'); recorded_round still closes the round; tests::unreported:2661 marks the hung test and every unreached test not_run, and tests::failed:2667 'not result["passed"] and not result.get("not_run")' excludes them. So unsettled_failures lists none (tests failures files no rerun), suite_reports ('if failed(result)') adds no report, and the stop itself is reported nowhere. settled_failures:3431 then prints ' ran in no round since whole-suite round N: run the whole suite again', and SKILL.md step 2a's last bullet answers 'run this step again', a whole round that stops at the same hang. Trigger: any test that hangs in sprint certification's suite. Harm (C1, work item 7: the find source the notes name, 'tests failures (schedule--, perf:, standing failures, not run)', and 'repeats until a whole-suite round passes after the last change'): the final whole-suite round reruns without end, no defect, report, or fixer names the hang, and certification never reaches its return. body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_write. What it does: takes the --after list as its parameter 'after', then rebinds the name inside the scenario loop (tests:3978 'after = [latest_support[path] for path in support_of(plan, s) if path in latest_support]') and the blocked-on-support loop (tests:4011 'after = {latest_support[path] ...}'); the closing pass (tests:4014-4016 'filing["after"] = sorted(set(filing["after"]) | set(after))') adds the last loop value, not the --after list, to every new filing. Trigger: tests tasks --stage write --after <code-stage build tasks> on a plan that writes a scenario (the boilerplate's step 4). Harm (C1, B121 / work item 6, the test stages chained behind the code stages): (a) the last scenario has no support file, so --after is dropped and every support, test, and legacy task is ready beside the code stages it tests; (b) its support file gets a support task in the same call, so its placeholder (e.g. '+0') joins every filing, the support task's own included, and the tracker refuses 'waits on +0, which does not exist', so the write stage files nothing; (c) every new filing waits on one unrelated support task and --after is still dropped. Scope: caused; the base stage_write took no --after. Reports: i41.
note: scripts/tests::stage_write: renamed the two loop locals that rebound the --after parameter (the scenario loop's support waits and the blocked-on-support refile waits) to 'waits', so the closing pass 'filing["after"] | set(after)' adds the --after list the caller gave to every new filing, never the last loop value; given_after_refusals and stage_preflight already read the parameter before the loops. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:suite_reports (with unsettled_failures, settled_failures, and skills/converge/SKILL.md Loop 2 step 2a). What it does: when a test hangs, read_stream stops the whole-suite round after testing.silence (found['stopped']='silence'); recorded_round still closes the round; tests::unreported:2661 marks the hung test and every unreached test not_run, and tests::failed:2667 'not result["passed"] and not result.get("not_run")' excludes them. So unsettled_failures lists none (tests failures files no rerun), suite_reports ('if failed(result)') adds no report, and the stop itself is reported nowhere. settled_failures:3431 then prints '<sids> ran in no round since whole-suite round N: run the whole suite again', and SKILL.md step 2a's last bullet answers 'run this step again', a whole round that stops at the same hang. Trigger: any test that hangs in sprint certification's suite. Harm (C1, work item 7: the find source the notes name, 'tests failures (schedule--, perf:, standing failures, not run)', and 'repeats until a whole-suite round passes after the last change'): the final whole-suite round reruns without end, no defect, report, or fixer names the hang, and certification never reaches its return. The sprint's 'not run' ruling (no fixer per unreached test) stands; the stopped round itself goes unreported. Scope: caused; the suite as a find source, settled, step 2a, and B13 are new in this sprint. Reports: i33 (and i46 in sprint-12).

Readings: (a) the plan or the stamp writes an unguarded entry {story, reason} for each planned story left with no scenario, which offers already reads; (b) offers reads the story's test stamp as the record of the plan that planned it, so a stamped story with no recorded scenario is not untested, and one whose file changed since that stamp is stale, as scenario-list-decided-once defines stale ('its file's blob id differs from its test stamp'). Built (b): a story entry never clears when the story's file changes, so (a) would hide a changed story from every later offer.

- i79: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md:step 10 and plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/test-legacy.md:Record. The completion report renders ## Stages from build tasks and ## Calls from the divergences pool; a legacy task records each port in the ports pool and records no item at all for a deletion (only its close result counts them). Trigger: a sprint takes a legacy group and its legacy tasks delete and port tests. Harm (A8, decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically: 'The completion report lists each deletion and each port for the owner's veto'): the report lists no deletion and no port, so the owner cannot veto a wrong deletion before the archive. Evidence: sprint-document.md:283-285; test-legacy.md:24 'Per deletion: delete the test.' with no record; test-legacy.md:34 'Per port: tasks item add --pool ports'; driver's archived run rendered '## Stages / None. / ## Calls / None.' after t1 closed 'tests/test_internal.py: 0 ported, 1 deleted' and t2 '1 ported, 0 deleted'. Failure i62.
- i86: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_sprint/shared.md:TEST-WASTE-RULE. What it does: the block restates the testing standard's named wastes for the planners and verifiers that include it, and its setup waste reads 'Setup a test repeats that it could share safely, such as a sign-in or a stack per test.' (shared.md:763-764). Work item 16 changed the standard: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/docs/testing.md:46-48 now reads 'Setup a test repeats that it could share safely, such as a sign-in or a stack per test, or data the test only reads that the project's seed could hold.', and the ambient copy plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/docs/plumbline-cheatsheet.md:148 carries the same clause. Trigger: any planner or verifier whose prompt includes {{TEST-WASTE-RULE}}. Harm (A8, .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md rule 1: a definition changed and a site that restates it left in the old form; rule 6.3): the restated list omits the seed waste, so a planner plans, and a verifier accepts, a test that rebuilds read-only data the seed could hold. Scope: caused; the change edited the standard's list and left this restatement as it stood at the base. From report i3.
- i87: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_sprint/shared.md:TEST-CALL-RULE. What it does: the block defines the call kind 'scope' as '`scope`: it reads the plan's scope or what a story covers.' (shared.md:647), and plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:551 keeps 'scope' in CALL_KINDS. Work item 3 retired the plan's scope: the sprint's notes say 'The /plan-tests scope question and the scope pool retire' and 'The scope item retires, so no in_scope refusals remain' (cmd_plan, B113); nothing else in the family names a plan's scope any more (rg "plan's scope" finds only shared.md:647). Trigger: every test planner whose prompt includes {{TEST-CALL-RULE}} sorts its calls by these kinds. Harm (A8, .claude/rules/plumbline-coding.md rule 1: a retired definition left restated in a template): the rule tells planners a call kind exists for reading a plan scope the plan no longer has, so the kind's definition describes a retired mechanism. Scope: caused; the change retired the scope and left this definition. From report i5.
- i90: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:speed_settled. What it does: for a latest speed verdict of product-slow it returns 'latest["id"] not in accepted_fixes(fixes)', and speed_rows passes fixes = run_items(root, run, "fixes") (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:4268); accepted_fixes reads accepted 'fixes' pool items carrying 'perf' (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:4187-4188). Nothing in the tree writes a 'fixes' pool item now: a perf: fix lands as a certification ledger defect whose test is perf:<sid>:<item>, set verified; perf_failures honors that (defect_tests(ledger_defects(root, sprint), VERIFIED), plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:4240) but speed_settled does not. Trigger: a speed reviewer records product-slow and certification verifies the perf: fix. Harm (C1, work item 10: 'it settles once its fix is accepted, and the test gets a fresh speed read'): speed_settled stays True for that test for the rest of the sprint, so tests slowest and --stage speed never give the fixed test its fresh speed read. Reports: i16, i18.

New perf_scenario(sid, item_id) builds the perf:<sid>:<item> id, used by perf_failure and speed_settled. So a verified perf: fix gives the test its fresh speed read in slowest and --stage speed. - i97: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_write. What it does: it takes the --after list as its parameter 'after', then rebinds the name in the scenario loop ('after = [latest_support[path] for path in support_of(plan, s) if path in latest_support]', plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:3978) and the blocked-on-support loop ('after = {latest_support[path] ...}' / 'after |= {...}', plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:4011-4012); the closing pass ('filing["after"] = sorted(set(filing["after"]) | set(after))', plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:4014-4016) adds the last loop value, not the caller's --after. Trigger: boilerplate step 4's --stage write --after <build tasks> on a plan that writes a scenario. Harm (C1, work item 6 / B121, test stages follow the code stages they test): where the last scenario names no support, --after is dropped and the test tasks run beside the code stages they test; where it names a support file planned in the same call, the placeholder '+0' joins every filing, the tracker refuses 'waits on +0, which does not exist', and the write stage files nothing. Report: i26.
- i98: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/test-speed.md, the Send back record. What it says: 'send the test back to a test task through its scenario's latest item in the tests pool ... Set the latest one for the scenario: tasks item set <item> --state sent-back', with no step where the pool holds no item for the scenario. A carried test from the ranking in test-state.json (--stage speed --from state) that no test task of this sprint wrote has no tests item in the run; plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:refiled_tests reads only tests-pool items (sent_back_tests over recorded_tests, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:3784-3812), so no rewrite is filed; stage_speed then skips the scenario (awaits_rewrite) and tests settled counts it settled while the file stands at its blob. note: scripts/tests: unsettled_failures no longer reads leftovers--, stopped--, and schedule-- entries from rounds[-1] alone. New standing_entries(rounds, schedule) walks every round since the latest closed whole-suite round, as standing_results does for tests: each round's entry failures (new entry_failures, also used by round_failures) stand, tagged with their round, until a later closed round reached the tests the entry concerns without reporting it again (entry_tests: the pair for schedule--, the unreached tests for stopped--, the reporting round's planned tests for leftovers--; entry_cleared: both of the pair, or any of the others). So a confirm rerun whose count grew again or that ran a and b together again keeps its entry listed when another confirm rerun of other tests ends later, and step 6a sends the defect back instead of setting it verified. The failures help text says the entries come from each round since the whole-suite round. Enumeration: callers of unsettled_failures are failing_targets, cmd_failures, settled_failures; all read the list unchanged in shape (entries gain a round field, which cmd_failures already prints). SKILL.md step 6a needed no change. File: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests

body: scripts/tests:standing_entries; which later round clears a leftovers--/stopped--/schedule-- entry. Readings: (a) a later closed round that reached any test the entry concerns (the reporting round's planned tests for leftovers, its unreached tests for stopped, both tests of the pair for schedule); (b) a round whose tests match the ledger defect's tests field; (c) never before the next whole-suite round. Built (a): it keeps a fixed defect's own confirm rerun able to clear the entry and stops an unrelated rerun from clearing it.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md:archive step 4 and plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:cmd_stamp. Certification runs the whole recorded suite for a sprint with no -plan.json (tests run reads it as a plan of no tests) and records its seconds and any speed acceptances, but the stamp that carries them into test-state.json runs only where -plan.json stands, and cmd_stamp calls read_plan, which refuses with no plan. Trigger: testing on, a sprint with nothing to plan, archived. Harm (A8, decision tests-spend-time-only-on-their-outcome: 'A passing whole-suite round ends a sprint's speed work, and its seconds feed the next sprint's ranking' and 'A speed acceptance ... holds across sprints until the test's own file changes'): the round's seconds never reach the ranking and its acceptances are never stamped, so the next sprint ranks on older rounds and re-reads accepted tests. Evidence: sprint-document.md:400 'Where <sprint-name>-plan.json stands beside the archived sprint, run .ok-planner/bin/tests stamp'; scripts/tests:4618 'plan = read_plan(root, sprint)'; scripts/tests:1154 'raise InputError("no plan at %s ...'. Failure i57.

In a scratch project (testing on, no -plan.json), tests run --sprint recorded a whole-suite round; after archiving, tests stamp exited 0: 'ranking: 2 tests; acceptances: 1; reaches: 0 tests', carrying the round's seconds and the run's speed acceptance into test-state.json, unguarded and kept preserved. The next sprint's tests slowest --from state ranked from it and left out the accepted test: '1 unsettled tests ... 2. s-b ... median 0.25s'.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:offer_groups. The untested offer counts a story untested where it has no recorded scenario and no unguarded entry names it by a story field, but no writer ever sets that field: plan assembly appends only {path, reason} for a no-guard program answer. Trigger: a sprint takes a story whose benefit only prose carries; its planner records no scenario and an untested call; the plan passes, tests stamp stamps the story. Harm (A3): the next tests offers offers the stamped story again as 'no recorded scenario', in every later sprint, so the untested offer never empties and the owner re-plans it for nothing; the story's 'reaches full coverage' is never reached. Evidence: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:899 'answered = {entry.get("story") for entry in state["unguarded"] if entry.get("story")}'; plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:1855 'unguarded.append({"path": text_field(answer, "path"), "reason": ...})'; driver saw 'untested:2: 1 untested stories / - gtc-s11: no recorded scenario' after 'story stamps: gtc-s11, gtc-s12'. Failures i52, i53 (one cause, two surfaces).
note: confirm drive: in a scratch project with 10 stories and testing on, tests offers printed untested:1 (gtc-s01..s08) and untested:2 (gtc-s09, gtc-s10); sprint 1 took untested:2 via tests groups --take, its story planner recorded both stories items with no scenario and untested calls, tests plan assembled (0 scenarios, calls: 2), tests stamp printed 'story stamps: gtc-s09, gtc-s10'; the next tests offers left both out and kept untested:1. Appending a line to gtc-s09.md made offers print 'stale:1: gtc-s09: its file changed since its test stamp 28145af...', gone once restored. Sprint 2 took untested:1 the same way; after its stamp, tests offers printed only the runtime group (no untested or stale group): full coverage reached one group at a time. skill:plan-sprint Frame shows the offers groups and passes taken keys to tests groups --take; text delivers.

body: In a scratch project (git init, true-up, two stories, '- No stack:' drive line, no commit yet) I ran the drive-mode verbs /converge's SKILL.md names in order: review stories, review drive-stack (none), tasks init, review prompt for each prompt, tasks round start, review drives, review merges --source drive, then Loop 2 step 3, review snapshot --out <folder>/fix-1.json; the story promises: 'to have each break that check finds fixed' whenever the owner chooses; saw: review snapshot exits 1 and the fix loop cannot start, and SKILL.md's Loop 2 step 3 names no route for a project whose repository has no commit; evidence: 'review: git diff --relative --name-status --no-renames HEAD -- . failed: fatal: bad revision 'HEAD'' exit 1; after one commit the same call printed 'snapshot: 0 file(s)' exit 0 and review fixes, review verifies, review drives --confirm --dry-run, and review drives --confirm each ran and filed as SKILL.md says
note: review-snapshot-fails-before-the-first-commit

body: Scratch repo project/ with the estate trued up at project/app (true-up wrote folders ["."]) and owned code at project/shared/util.py. Declared folders [".","../shared"]: review files, review changed, review areas, review checks, the lint, and the edit hook each reached ../shared/util.py. Then declared folders [".","../shared","../nope"] (one mistyped entry beside a valid one) and changed shared/util.py. The lint refuses that config (plumbline . exit 1: 'error: .ok-planner/config.json: folders[2] "../nope" is not an existing directory'), but the review tool proceeds with a code default: review changed printed 'review: .ok-planner/config.json sets a malformed folders, so the review reads the project root alone; run /ok, which repairs it:' then only 'changed .ok-planner/config.json', exit 0, leaving out the changed ../shared/util.py that the valid entry declares; review files and review areas likewise listed only main.py and the two config files, exit 0 (areas.json files: ['.ok-planner/config.json', '.ok-planner/review/config.json', 'main.py']). With the good config the same review changed printed 'changed ../shared/util.py'. The story promises: no check the suite runs over my project misses code I own; decision project-declares-its-folders says every tool reads the one list so the lint and review do not drift, and settings-have-no-code-defaults says code that finds a setting unusable refuses rather than defaulting. Saw: one mistyped entry makes every /converge mode's file population (hunt areas, sprint changed files, review checks) silently drop every declared folder and run exit 0 on the root alone, while the lint refuses the same config; evidence quoted above.
note: review-reads-root-alone-on-one-bad-folder

body: Reviewed /plan-docs (SKILL.md steps 2-7), its doc-sprint template, and scripts/docs, then ran them in a scratch project (stack run keep-documentation-current-eedeaa6d): committed tool.py --bye, planned a documentation sprint at e55fcf1 (Window line 'Planned against commit e55fcf1'), then committed tool.py --loud before execution, recorded the base per step 3, ran writer/style/checker tasks, archived, committed, and ran 'docs stamp'. The story promises: after each update a reader finds documentation that describes the product as it stands. Saw: nothing compares the run's base with the planned commit. Step 3 of the template only says 'Where git status --porcelain lists a path outside .ok-planner/, name those paths to the owner and stop. Otherwise write the output of git rev-parse HEAD to the file beside this one', and 'docs stamp' (cmd_stamp) sets state['stamp'] = args.commit for every planned docspec. So a product change committed between the plan and its execution, which no planner saw and no item carries, is stamped over: the next window reports the docspec current. Evidence: after the stamp, 'docs window' printed 'docspec:guide stamp: 4bdee14e... status: current' and 'docspec:faq stamp: 4bdee14e... status: current', while 'grep -c loud docs/guide.md docs/faq.md' printed 0 for a tool that now takes --loud. The update hides the gap from every later run.
note: doc-sprint-stamps-over-commits-after-its-plan

body: .ok-planner/review/project.md, Scripts for developers and operators, tests bullet: 'stamp --sprint <archived path> --commit <sha> writes the scenario list a sprint archived under .ok-planner/history/sprints/ with its -plan.json leaves' no longer matches the tool after i69: stamp now takes a sprint with no -plan.json as a plan of no tests and writes its ranking, acceptances, and reaches. A driver reading the facts would expect a refusal (A9-adjacent stale fact; fix the sentence).
note: review-facts-say-tests-stamp-needs-a-plan

body: ok-setup/SKILL.md 3.5, the veto of the budget agent's calls (i78). Readings: (a) after the budget is written, follow {{CEREMONY-VETO}} in _sprint/shared.md, filing each vetoed call as a ruled product-intent issue for the next /plan-sprint; (b) show the calls before the budget is written and refile the budget task with each vetoed row and the owner's words, so the veto takes effect in this session. Built (b): the owner is present, the budget is this session's own output, and the file already refiles the budget task for a budget that does not hold.
note: ok-setup-budget-veto-timing

body: admin/true-up::certified_mark_steps (i80); the choice: how to tell a sprint an earlier release certified from a live one. Readings: (a) true-up writes -certified.txt where the completion report holds '# Sprint certification' and the boilerplate holds a retired template line; (b) plumbline skips any sprint whose completion report holds the return block, which would close the window for a carried-release sprint whose certification printed SPRINT NOT COMPLETE; (c) leave it to the owner's archive. Built (a): it is a one-time migration of stored state, and its mark text says true-up wrote it under an earlier release.
note: earlier-release-sprints-marked-certified

body: scripts/tests::stopped_failures (i64): how a whole-suite round that stops on testing.silence is reported. Readings: (a) one round-level stopped--silence entry, class T1, naming the not-run tests, which a fixer narrows by running them alone (as leftovers-- is narrowed); (b) treat a lone missing test in a stopped round as failed and rerun every unreached test alone before reporting, which leaves a stop no lone run reproduces unreported; (c) a new T5 class in _sprint/shared.md. Built (a): it reports every stop, keeps the sprint's 'no fixer per unreached test' ruling, and needs no new class; shared.md's T1 row (held by t56) reads 'a test fails', which a hang is.
note: stopped-test-round-report-shape

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:offer_groups (i67); the choice: how a story a plan planned with no scenario leaves the untested offer. Readings: (a) the plan or the stamp writes an unguarded entry {story, reason} for each planned story left with no scenario, which offers already reads; (b) offers reads the story's test stamp as the record of the plan that planned it, so a stamped story with no recorded scenario is not untested, and one whose file changed since that stamp is stale, as scenario-list-decided-once defines stale ('its file's blob id differs from its test stamp'). Built (b): a story entry never clears when the story's file changes, so (a) would hide a changed story from every later offer.
note: planned-story-with-no-scenario-offered-as-untested

body: scripts/tests:standing_entries; which later round clears a leftovers--/stopped--/schedule-- entry. Readings: (a) a later closed round that reached any test the entry concerns (the reporting round's planned tests for leftovers, its unreached tests for stopped, both tests of the pair for schedule); (b) a round whose tests match the ledger defect's tests field; (c) never before the next whole-suite round. Built (a): it keeps a fixed defect's own confirm rerun able to clear the entry and stops an unrelated rerun from clearing it.
note: which-round-clears-a-round-level-test-entry
